   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:center;margin:0pt;"><b>(Dollars in thousands, except share and per share data)</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:center;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:center;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>&#8226; </b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em></b>: Inputs are unobservable for the asset or liability, and include situations where there is little, if any, market activity for the asset or liability. In certain cases, the inputs used to measure fair value <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>fall into different levels of the fair value hierarchy. In such cases, the level in the fair value hierarchy within which the fair value measurement in its entirety falls has been determined based on the lowest level input that is significant to the fair value measurement in its entirety. Our assessment of the significance of a particular input to the fair value measurement in its entirety requires judgment, and considers factors specific to the asset or liability.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The availability of observable inputs can vary depending on the financial asset or liability and is affected by a wide variety of factors, including, for example, the type of investment, whether the investment is new, whether the investment is traded on an active exchange or in the secondary market, and the current market condition. To the extent that valuation is based on models or inputs that are less observable or unobservable in the market, the determination of fair value requires more judgment. Accordingly, the degree of judgment exercised by us in determining fair value is greatest for instruments categorized in Level <em style="font: inherit;">3.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Fair value is a market-based measure considered from the perspective of a market participant who holds the asset or owes the liability rather than an entity-specific measure. Therefore, even when market assumptions are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> readily available, our own assumptions are set to reflect those that management believes market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability at the measurement date. We use prices and inputs that management believes are current as of the measurement date, including during periods of market dislocation. In periods of market dislocation, the observability of prices and inputs <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be reduced for many instruments. This condition could cause an instrument to be transferred from Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> to Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> or Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> to Level <em style="font: inherit;">3.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Fair value for certain of our Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> financial instruments is derived using internal valuation models. These internal valuation models include discounted cash flow analyses developed by management using current interest rates, estimates of the term of the particular instrument, specific issuer information and other market data for securities without an active market. In accordance with FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">820,</em> &#8220;Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures&#8221;, the impact of our own credit spreads is also considered when measuring the fair value of financial assets or liabilities. Where appropriate, valuation adjustments are made to account for various factors, including bid-ask spreads, credit quality and market liquidity. These adjustments are applied on a consistent basis and are based on observable inputs where available. Management&#8217;s estimate of fair value requires significant management judgment and is subject to a high degree of variability based upon market conditions, the availability of specific issuer information and management&#8217;s assumptions.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">825,</em> &#8220;Financial Instruments&#8221; requires disclosure of the fair value of financial instruments for which it is practicable to estimate that value. Given that cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash are short term in&#160;nature with limited fair value volatility, the carrying amount is deemed to be a reasonable approximation of fair value and the fair value input is classified as a Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> fair value measurement. The fair value input for derivatives is classified as a Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> fair value measurement within the fair value hierarchy. The fair value of our unsecured revolver, term loans, and mortgage indebtedness is based on a discounted cash flows valuation technique. As this technique utilizes current credit spreads, which are generally unobservable, this is classified as a Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> fair value measurement within the fair value hierarchy. We determine appropriate credit spreads based on the type of debt and its maturity. There were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> transfers between levels in the fair value hierarchy for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>. The following table summarizes the carrying amount and the fair value of our financial instruments as of the periods indicated:</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In addition to assets and liabilities that are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis, we record assets and liabilities at fair value on a nonrecurring basis as required by U.S. GAAP. Generally, assets are recorded at fair value on a nonrecurring basis as a result of impairment charges. As discussed further in Note <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> &#8220;Investments in Real Estate&#8221;, we recognized an aggregate impairment charge of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945382" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_FairValueByMeasurementFrequencyAxis-FairValueMeasurementsNonrecurringMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfRealEstate" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">12,841</ix:nonFraction> during the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> for <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of the properties&#160;that were&#160;held for sale as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. The impairment charge was determined by comparing the fair value of the property to its carrying value.&#160;The fair value&#160;was determined to be a Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> fair value measurement within the fair value hierarchy based on unobservable inputs through a direct capitalization valuation. Significant assumptions included a range of capitalization rates between <ix:nonFraction id="c139945385" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:FairValueAssumptionsCapitalizationRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">5.5</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction id="c139945386" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:FairValueAssumptionsCapitalizationRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">6.0</ix:nonFraction>% reflecting the current economic conditions. Our projections were based on current market conditions and internal assumptions, which could be impacted by future changes in the market.</p>

   </ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock" id="c139946055" escape="true"><table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 9pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>l.</i></b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Office Leases</i></b></p> </td></tr>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In accordance with FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">842,</em> &#8220;Leases&#8221;, lessees are required to recognize a right-of-use asset and a lease liability on the balance sheet at the lease commencement date for all leases, except those leases with terms of less than a year. We lease corporate office space under leases with terms of up to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" id="c139945389" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years and that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include extension options, but that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include any residual value guarantees or restrictive covenants. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, we have $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945392" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,771</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945393" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,877</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, of operating lease right-of-use assets and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c139945394" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseLiability" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">3,082</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945395" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseLiability" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,123</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, of operating lease liabilities related to our corporate office leases. The operating lease right-of-use assets are presented within <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139945970"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139945971">other assets</span></span> and the operating lease liabilities are presented within <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139945972"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139945973">other liabilities</span></span> in our consolidated balance sheet. We recorded $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945396" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">616</ix:nonFraction>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945397" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">674</ix:nonFraction>, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945398" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">849</ix:nonFraction>&#160;of total operating lease expense during the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, respectively, which is recorded within property management expense and general and administrative expenses in our consolidated statements of operations.</p>

   </ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c139946056" escape="true"><table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 9pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>m.</i></b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Income Taxes</i></b></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We have elected to be taxed as a REIT. Accordingly, we recorded <ix:nonFraction id="c139945401" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> income tax expense for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">To qualify as a REIT, we must meet certain organizational and operational requirements, including a requirement to distribute at least <em style="font: inherit;">90%</em> of our ordinary taxable income to stockholders. As a REIT, we generally are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to federal income tax on taxable income that we distribute to our stockholders. If we fail to qualify as a REIT in any taxable year, we will be subject to federal income taxes on our taxable income at regular corporate rates and will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be permitted to qualify for treatment as a REIT for federal income tax purposes for <em style="font: inherit;">four</em> years following the year during which qualification is lost unless the Internal Revenue Service grants us relief under certain statutory provisions. Such an event could materially adversely affect our net income and net cash available for distribution to stockholders; however, we believe that we are organized and operate in such a manner as to qualify and maintain treatment as a REIT and intend to operate in such a manner so that we will remain qualified as a REIT for federal income tax purposes.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">For the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, <ix:nonFraction id="c139945408" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:DividendsCharacterizedAsCapitalGainDistributionPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">42</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;of dividends were characterized as capital gain distributions and <ix:nonFraction id="c139945409" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:DividendsCharacterizedAsOrdinaryIncomePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">58</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;were characterized as ordinary income. For the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>, <ix:nonFraction id="c139945410" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:DividendsCharacterizedAsCapitalGainDistributionPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">88</ix:nonFraction>% of dividends were characterized as capital gain distributions and <ix:nonFraction id="c139945411" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:DividendsCharacterizedAsOrdinaryIncomePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">12</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;were characterized as ordinary income. For the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2023</em>, <ix:nonFraction id="c139945412" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:DividendsCharacterizedAsCapitalGainDistributionPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">74</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;of dividends were characterized as capital gain distributions, <ix:nonFraction id="c139945413" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:DividendsCharacterizedAsOrdinaryIncomePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">26</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;were characterized as ordinary income.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   </ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" id="c139946057" escape="true"><table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 9pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>n.</i></b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Share-Based Compensation</i></b></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We account for stock-based compensation in accordance with FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">718,</em> &#8220;Compensation - Stock Compensation&#8221;. Any stock-based compensation awards granted are measured based on the grant-date fair value of the award and compensation expense for the entire award is recognized on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period, which is the vesting period, for the entire award. Certain of our stock-based compensation awards provide for accelerated vesting upon retirement. In these cases, we recognize compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the period from grant date to the date the employee will become retirement eligible. If the grantee is retirement eligible at the time they receive an award, the full amount of compensation expense is recognized immediately on the grant date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   </ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationSubsidiariesOrOtherInvestmentsConsolidatedEntitiesPolicy" id="c139946058" escape="true"><table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 9pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>o.</i></b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Noncontrolling Interest</i></b></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Our noncontrolling interest represents limited partnership units of our operating partnership that were issued in connection with certain property acquisitions and a joint venture partner's interest of a consolidated joint venture. We record limited partnership units issued in an acquisition at their fair value on the closing date of the acquisition. The holders of the limited partnership units have the right to redeem their limited partnership units for either shares of our common stock or for cash at our discretion. As the settlement of a redemption is in our sole discretion, we present noncontrolling interest in our consolidated balance sheet within equity but separate from stockholders&#8217; equity. Any noncontrolling interests that fail to qualify as permanent equity will be presented as temporary equity and be carried at the greater of historical cost or their redemption value.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   </ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:DerivativesPolicyTextBlock" id="c139946059" escape="true"><table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 9pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>p.</i></b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Derivative Instruments</i></b></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>use derivative financial instruments to hedge all or a portion of the interest rate risk associated with our borrowings. The principal objective of such arrangements is to minimize the risks and/or costs associated with our operating and financial structure, as well as, to hedge specific anticipated transactions. While these instruments <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>impact our periodic cash flows, they benefit us by minimizing the risks and/or costs previously described. The counterparties to these contractual arrangements are major financial institutions with which we and our affiliates <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also have other financial relationships. In the event of nonperformance by the counterparties, we are potentially exposed to credit loss. However, because of the high credit ratings of the counterparties, we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> anticipate that any of the counterparties will fail to meet their obligations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In accordance with FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">815,</em> &#8220;Derivatives and Hedging&#8221;, we measure each derivative instrument (including any derivative instruments embedded in other contracts) at fair value and record such amounts in our&#160;consolidated balance sheet as either an asset or liability. For derivatives designated as cash flow hedges, the changes in the fair value of the effective portions of the derivative are reported in other comprehensive income (loss) and changes in the ineffective portions of cash flow hedges, if any, are recognized in earnings. For derivatives <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedges, the changes in fair value of the derivative instrument are recognized in earnings. Any derivatives that we designate in hedge relationships are done so at inception. At inception, we determine whether or <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> the derivative is highly effective in offsetting changes in the designated interest rate risk associated with the identified indebtedness using regression analysis. At each reporting period, we update our regression analysis and use the hypothetical derivative method to measure any ineffectiveness.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   </ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="irt:EmployeeRetentionCreditPolicyTextBlock" id="c139946060" escape="true"><table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 9pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>q.</i></b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Employee Retention Credit</i></b></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Under the terms of the <em style="font: inherit;"> March 27, 2020 </em>Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act (&#8220;CARES Act&#8221;), we were eligible and applied for assistance in the form of a refundable employee retention credit. Since applicable GAAP guidance is limited, we adopted an accounting policy by analogizing to International Accounting Standard <em style="font: inherit;">20</em> &#8220;Accounting for Government Grants&#8221; to recognize employee retention credits as a reimbursement of payroll related expenses within property operating expenses, property management expenses, and general and administrative expenses in our consolidated statements of operations. During the years&#160;ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em>&#160;we recognized reimbursements of payroll related expenses of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945422" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="irt:ProceedsFromRetentionCreditRefunds" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0</ix:nonFraction>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945423" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="irt:ProceedsFromRetentionCreditRefunds" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945424" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="irt:ProceedsFromRetentionCreditRefunds" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">3,232</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, in our consolidated statements of operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>

   </ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:CostsAssociatedWithExitOrDisposalActivitiesOrRestructuringsPolicy" id="c139946061" escape="true"><table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 9pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>r.</i></b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Restructuring Costs</i></b></p> </td></tr>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2023, </em>we reorganized certain departments in our organization impacting a limited number of employees. The impacted employees were provided severance packages that included cash severance payments and the accelerated vesting of performance share units and restricted stock awards, as applicable. In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">712</em> &#8220;Compensation &#8211; Nonretirement Postemployment Benefits&#8221;, we recognized the full amount of restructuring costs of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945428" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCharges" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">3,213</ix:nonFraction> during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2023, </em>which is presented in the restructuring costs line on the consolidated statement of operations. <ix:nonFraction id="c139945430" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCharges" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">No</ix:nonFraction> restructuring costs were recognized during the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025&#160;</em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   </ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c139946062" escape="true"><table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 9pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>s.</i></b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Recent Accounting Pronouncements</i></b></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Below is a brief description of recent accounting pronouncements that could have a material effect on our financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">12</em><i>, Codification Improvements</i>, as part of its ongoing project to clarify, correct and improve various topics within the Accounting Standards Codification (ASC). The amendments cover <em style="font: inherit;">33</em> specific issues, <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> of which are particularly relevant to REITs, (i)&#160;clarifications on the calculation of diluted earnings per share when a loss from continuing operations exists (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">260</em>) and (ii) the exclusion of certain lease receivables from enhanced credit loss disclosures (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">310</em>). The standard is effective for the Company for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim periods within those years. Early adoption is permitted on an issue-by-issue basis. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">12</em> on its consolidated financial position, results of operations and disclosures.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em> <i>Derivatives and Hedging (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">815</em>): Hedge Accounting Improvements</i>. The update is designed to better align hedge accounting with an entity's risk management activities by making targeted improvements to the hedge accounting model. Key amendments include,&#160;Similar Risk Assessment, which replaces the &#8220;shared risk exposure&#8221; requirement for grouping forecasted transactions in a cash flow hedge with a &#8220;similar risk exposure&#8221; requirement, permitting broader aggregation of hedged risks, Choose-Your-Rate Debt which introduces a model for hedging interest payments on variable-rate borrowings where the borrower can change reference rates without automatically triggering hedge de-designation, and Net Written Options which clarifies that certain instruments, such as, interest rate swaps with floors, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>qualify as hedging instruments without being subject to the net written option test, provided.&#160;The standard is effective for the Company for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim periods within those years. Early adoption is permitted. The guidance is generally required to be applied on a prospective basis. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em>&#160;on its consolidated financial position, results of operations and disclosures.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> March 2024, </em>the SEC issued rules on the enhancement and standardization of climate-related disclosures. The rules, require disclosure of material climate-related risks; activities to mitigate or adapt to such risks; governance and management of such risks; and material greenhouse gas emissions from operations owned or controlled and or indirect emissions from purchased energy consumed in operations. Additionally, the rules require disclosure in the notes to the financial statements of the effects of severe weather events and other natural conditions, subject to certain materiality thresholds. The rules were to&#160;become effective for the Company starting in the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025. </em>While the SEC has voluntarily stayed the rules, the Company is currently evaluating the effect the rules will have on its financial statement disclosures.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Sixth Restated Credit Agreement contains customary covenants for credit facilities of this type, including restrictions on our ability to take the following actions: (i) make distributions after an event of default; (ii) incur debt; (iii) make investments; (iv) grant or suffer liens; (v) undertake mergers, consolidations, asset sales and other fundamental entity changes; (vi) make material changes to contracts and organizational documents; and (vii) enter into transactions with affiliates.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Sixth Restated Credit Agreement also contains financial covenants applicable to us involving (i) maximum consolidated total debt to total asset value, (ii) maximum distributions, (iii) maximum secured debt to total asset value, (iv) maximum unsecured debt to eligible unencumbered properties, and (v) minimum consolidated fixed charge coverage. The Sixth Restated Credit Agreement provides for certain customary events of default, including among others, non-payment of principal, interest or other amounts when due, inaccuracy of representations and warranties, violation of covenants, cross defaults with certain other indebtedness, insolvency or inability to pay debts, bankruptcy, or a change of control.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> August 6, 2025, </em>we entered into a forward interest rate swap contract with a notional value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945625" contextRef="i_2025-08-06_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-ForwardInterestRateSwapMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">150,000</ix:nonFraction>, a strike rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c139945626" contextRef="i_2025-08-06_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-ForwardInterestRateSwapMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:DerivativeStrikeRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">3.26</ix:nonFraction>% and a maturity date of <em style="font: inherit;"> June 17, 2030. </em>The interest rate swap has an effective date of <em style="font: inherit;"> June 17, 2026. </em>We designated this interest rate swap as a cash flow hedge at inception and determined that the hedge is highly effective in offsetting interest rate fluctuations associated with the identified indebtedness.</p>

As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945687" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtMarketProgramMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">342,400</ix:nonFraction>&#160;remained available for issuance under our&#160;ATM Program.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2024, </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em>we entered into forward sales transactions under the ATM Program for the forward sale of an aggregate of <ix:nonFraction id="c139945689" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtMarketProgramMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,498,300</ix:nonFraction> shares of our common stock with a maturity date of <em style="font: inherit;"> September 5, 2025 </em>or <em style="font: inherit;"> November 13, 2025, </em>respectively, as set forth in the forward sale transactions placement notice. On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 30, 2024, </em>we physically settled all of these <ix:nonFraction id="c139945690" contextRef="i_2024-12-30_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtMarketProgramMember" unitRef="Share" name="irt:EquitySharesSettled" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,498,300</ix:nonFraction> shares of our common stock at a weighted average price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945691" contextRef="i_2024-12-30_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtMarketProgramMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:SharesIssuedPricePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">20.06</ix:nonFraction> per share and we received net proceeds of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945692" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-30_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtMarketProgramMember" unitRef="USD" name="irt:SaleOfStockSettlementValueOfShares" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">50,106</ix:nonFraction>. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em>approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945693" contextRef="i_2024-12-30_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtMarketProgramMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">399,435</ix:nonFraction> remained available for issuance under our ATM Program.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We evaluated the accounting for the forward sale transactions under FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">480</em> &#8220;Distinguishing Liabilities from Equity&#8221; and FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">815</em> &#8220;Derivatives and Hedging&#8221;. As the forward sale transactions are&#160;considered indexed to our own equity and since they meet the equity classification conditions in ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">25,</em> the forward sale transactions have been classified as equity.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Stock Repurchase Program</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 18, 2022, </em>our Board of Directors authorized a common stock repurchase program (the &#8220;Stock Repurchase Program&#8221;) covering the repurchase of up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945700" contextRef="i_2022-05-18" unitRef="USD" name="srt:StockRepurchaseProgramAuthorizedAmount1" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">250,000</ix:nonFraction> in shares of our common stock. Under the Stock Repurchase Program, we, in our discretion, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>purchase our shares from time to time in the open market or in privately negotiated transactions. The amount and timing of the purchases of our common stock will depend on a number of factors, including the price and availability of our shares of common stock, trading volumes and general market conditions. The Stock Repurchase Program has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> time limit and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be suspended or discontinued at any time. During the year&#160;ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, we repurchased and retired <ix:nonFraction id="c139945702" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedAndRetiredDuringPeriodShares" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,872,684</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock under our&#160;Stock Repurchase Program at a weighted average price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945703" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:SharesRepurchasedAveragePricePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">16.00</ix:nonFraction>&#160;per share at&#160;a total cost of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945704" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedAndRetiredDuringPeriodValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">30,000</ix:nonFraction>.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">8:</em> Equity Compensation Plans</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 18, 2022, </em>our stockholders approved our <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Long Term Incentive Plan (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2022</em> Incentive Plan&#8221;) which replaced the <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em> Long Term Incentive Plan (the &#8220;Prior Plan&#8221;, collectively with the <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Incentive Plan, the &#8220;Incentive Plan&#8221;). <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> new awards <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be made under the Prior Plan, although awards outstanding under the Prior Plan will remain subject to the terms of the Prior Plan. The <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Incentive Plan provides for grants of equity and equity-based awards to our employees, officers, directors, consultants and other service providers, and such awards <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>take the form of restricted or unrestricted shares of common stock, non-qualified stock options, incentive stock options, restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;), stock appreciation rights (&#8220;SARs&#8221;), dividend equivalents and other equity and cash-based awards. A maximum of <ix:nonFraction id="c139945727" contextRef="i_2022-05-18_PlanNameAxis-LongTermIncentivePlanMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">8,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of our common stock (plus up to an additional <ix:nonFraction id="c139945728" contextRef="d_2022-05-18_2022-05-18_PlanNameAxis-LongTermIncentivePlanMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Share" name="irt:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardNumberOfAdditionalSharesPotentiallyRecycledIntoTheStockPlan" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,280,610</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of our common stock, to the extent that shares subject to outstanding awards under the Prior Plan are recycled into the <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Incentive Plan) <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be awarded under the <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Incentive Plan, subject to customary adjustment for stock splits, reverse stock splits and similar corporate events or transactions affecting shares of our common stock.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Under the Incentive Plan, we have granted restricted shares, RSUs, and performance share units (&#8220;PSUs&#8221;). For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> we recognized $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945733" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">8,276</ix:nonFraction>,&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c139945734" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">7,390</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c139945735" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">7,883</ix:nonFraction>&#160;of stock compensation expense, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The restricted shares and RSUs granted under the Incentive Plan generally vest over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139945994">two</span>, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139945995">three</span>, or <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139945736">four</span>-year period. In addition, we have granted unrestricted shares to our non-employee directors. These awards generally vest or vested immediately. A summary of restricted common share award and RSU activity is presented below.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The PSUs granted under the Incentive Plan have a <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-year performance period and are generally based on (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) market performance as measured by total stockholder return for <ix:nonFraction id="c139945759" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceShareUnitsPsusMember" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardPerformanceRightsByShareHolderReturnPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">70</ix:nonFraction>% of the award and (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) a subjective element tied to individual performance for <ix:nonFraction id="c139945761" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceShareUnitsPsusMember" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardPerformanceRightsByIndividualCriteriaPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">30</ix:nonFraction>% of the award. The PSUs vest <ix:nonFraction id="c139945762" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_VestingAxis-ShareBasedCompensationAwardTrancheOneMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">50</ix:nonFraction>% upon the Compensation Committee&#8217;s determination as to the satisfaction of the performance criteria (which shall be within <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> months of the last day of the performance period) and <ix:nonFraction id="c139945764" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_VestingAxis-ShareBasedCompensationAwardTrancheTwoMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">50</ix:nonFraction>% on the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> anniversary of the last day of the performance period, subject to continued service through such dates. A summary of PSU activity is presented below.</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3103830" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">11:</em> Segment Reporting</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Each of our multifamily properties is considered an operating segment that earns revenues through the leasing of apartment homes and incurs associated expenses. Individual operating results for each of our multifamily properties is reviewed and discrete financial information is available. Our multifamily properties have similar long-term economic characteristics and provide similar products and services to a similar class of residents. All operations are within the United States and <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> individual multifamily property comprises more than <em style="font: inherit;">10%</em> of consolidated revenues or assets. We aggregate our multifamily properties on a same-store and non same-store basis, and as a result, have identified <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139945795">two</span> reportable segments.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 54pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#8226;</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Same-Store includes properties that were owned and <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a development property as of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2024, </em>and that have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been sold or identified as held for sale.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 54pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#8226;</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Non Same-Store includes properties that did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet the definition of a same-store property as of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2024.</em></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">GAAP guidance requires that segment disclosures present the measures used by the Chief Operating Decision Maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;) to decide how to allocate resources and for purposes of assessing segment performance. As a group, our executive officers, including the CEO, President and CFO, CAO, and EVP of Operations act as the CODM. The CODM manages and reviews our operations on both a property-by-property basis and same-store and non same-store basis and uses net operating income (&#8220;NOI&#8221;) as the primary financial measure to evaluate operating results of our multifamily properties, including analyses compared to prior periods and budgeted operating results. NOI is defined as total property revenues less total property operating expenses, excluding interest expenses, depreciation and amortization, casualty related costs and gains, property management expenses, general and administrative expense, net gains on sale of assets&#160;and restructuring costs.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Segment assets consist of real estate held for investment, real estate held for sale and investments in real estate under development. Non-segment assets consist of assets in the Company&#8217;s other non-reportable segments and corporate non-segment assets, which are comprised of cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, investments in unconsolidated real estate entities, other assets, derivative assets and intangible assets. Reportable segment asset information is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> provided to the CODM as the CODM does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> use segment asset information to evaluate the business and allocate resources.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">12:</em> Commitments and Contingencies</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Litigation</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We are subject to various legal proceedings and claims that arise in the ordinary course of our business operations. Matters which arise out of allegations of bodily injury, property damage, and employment practices are generally covered by insurance. While the resolution of these matters cannot be predicted with certainty, we currently believe the final outcome of such matters will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material adverse effect on our financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Starting around <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2022, </em>putative class action representatives began filing complaints in various United States District Courts across the country naming as defendants RealPage, Inc. ("RealPage"), a seller of revenue management products, and approximately <em style="font: inherit;">50</em> defendants who own and/or manage multifamily residential rental housing, alleging that the defendants conspired to fix, raise, maintain, and stabilize rent prices in violation of Section <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> of the Sherman Act. Some of the complaints, including <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> filed on <em style="font: inherit;"> November 14, 2022, </em>in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, named us as <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of the defendants, and others did <em style="font: inherit;">not.</em> Discovery is ongoing. It is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> possible for the Company to estimate the amount of loss, if&#160; any, which <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be associated with an adverse decision in this matter. We deny all allegations of wrongdoing and intend to defend against these claims vigorously. See &#8220;Part I. Item <em style="font: inherit;">3.</em> Legal Proceedings.&#8221;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Other Matters</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">To the extent that a natural disaster or similar event occurs with more than a remote risk of having a material impact on the consolidated financial statements, we will disclose the estimated range of possible outcomes, and, if an outcome is probable, accrue an appropriate liability.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Lease Obligations</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We lease office space in Philadelphia, PA , Chicago, IL and Tampa, FL.   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><a id="changes" href="#"></a>ITEM 9.</b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b><i>Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">None.</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 16pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><a id="controls" href="#"></a>ITEM 9A.</b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b><i>Controls and Procedures</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b>Disclosure Controls and Procedures</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We maintain disclosure controls and procedures that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in our reports under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;), is recorded, processed, summarized, and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#8217;s rules and forms, and that such information is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our chief executive officer and our chief financial officer, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. In designing and evaluating the disclosure controls and procedures, our management recognized that any controls and procedures, no matter how well designed and operated, can provide only reasonable assurance of achieving the desired control objectives, and our management necessarily was required to apply its judgment in evaluating the cost-benefit relationship of possible controls and procedures.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Under the supervision of our chief executive officer and chief financial officer and with the participation of our disclosure committee, we have carried out an evaluation of the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures as of the end of the period covered by this report. Based upon that evaluation, our chief executive officer and chief financial officer determined that, as of December 31, 2025, our disclosure controls and procedures are effective at the reasonable assurance level.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b>Management</b>&#8217;<b>s Annual Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting as defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act. Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risks that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Management assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025. In making this assessment, management used the criteria set forth by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) in <i>Internal Control </i>&#8211;<i> Integrated Framework </i>(2013 Framework).<i> </i>Based on this assessment, management believes that, as of December 31, 2025, our internal control over financial reporting is effective.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Our independent registered public accounting firm has issued an attestation report on our internal control over financial reporting. This report is included as part of Item 8 in this annual report on Form 10-K.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b>Changes in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">There were no changes in our internal control over financial reporting or in other factors during our last fiscal quarter that have materially affected, or were reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
